🇵🇸 After enduring genocide, displaced Palestinians in Gaza are now facing torrential rain and flooding in the camps where they sought shelter. In its October 26 report, the UN's independent commission of inquiry said the genocide was ongoing. On November 7, Gaza's Civil Defence reported around 1,500 calls for help in just 10 hours. The Hamas-run government media office estimated that around 70,000 tents flooded in 12 hours. Before the storm, the UN had already warned of shortages of tents, tarps and blankets. Israeli restrictions on the entry of shelter supplies and funding shortfalls had hampered preparations for winter. Families need waterproof shelters, dry blankets and pumps to drain the flooded camps. Those forced out of their tents need somewhere safe to sleep tonight. #Gaza #freepalestine #freepalestine🇵🇸❤️ #Palestine #palestine🇵🇸

She's holding her doll tight because it's the only thing that hasn't left her. No shoes. No clean clothes. No safe home. This is what the world has allowed childhood to become in Palestine. Say her name in your prayers. Share her story. Israeli Forces Block Palestinian-American From Entering His Home After Returning From the US in Turmus Ayya Israeli forces prevented a Palestinian-American citizen arriving from the United States from entering his family home in the town of Turmus Ayya, north of Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank. According to local reports, the home has been under Israeli military occupation for 17 consecutive days, leaving the family unable to return to their property. Despite travelling thousands of miles back from the United States, the Palestinian-American man was denied access to his own home.
